Facts: Plaintiff-heir via 2017 holographic will challenged 2019 public will appointing defendant sole heir; claimed formal-defects (unsigned first-page violating notarial-law, inadequate wishes-investigation given ten-minute drafting), virtual-nullity (concrete-cause lack), annulment for testamentary-incapacity; defendant contested claiming will valid, plaintiff-claim inadmissible absent mediation-attempt; parish intervened endorsing plaintiff-claims.
Legal Framework: Articles 603, 606 Italian Civil Code (public-will formalities; nullity/annulment grounds); Royal Decree 89/1913 Arts. 47, 51(2)(12), 58, 60, 67 (notarial-law provisions); Art. 2700 Civil Code (public-document proof-effect); case law on public-will signature-requirements, notary wishes-investigation, incapacity-proof burden (Cass. 1649/2017, 9081/2010, 28758/2017).
Interpretive Issues: Whether first-page signature-absence constitutes form-defect when page contains only preliminary-checks not testamentary-dispositions; adequacy-standard for notary wishes-investigation when brief time-elapsed between receipt/document-preparation; virtual-nullity applicability when concrete-cause allegedly unascertained; burden-proof allocation for testamentary-incapacity challenging public-will presuming capacity-absence; admissibility of medical-psychiatric expert when exploratory; public-document faith-effect on incapacity-perception.
Principles Applied: Public-will nullity-grounds: notary/testator signature-failure (Art. 606(1)); witness signature-failure merely annulment-ground. Any other form-defect may render will annullable per Art. 606(2). Plaintiff invokes annulment per Art. 606(2) combined Art. 51(2)(12) RD 89/1913. First-page signature-lack complaint rejected; signature-rationale satisfied: testator-signature appears second-page (reproducing testamentary-wishes) and third-page (containing final-signatures witnesses/notary). Signature serves certifying expressed-will finality drawing testator-attention to testament; multi-sheet will requires each-sheet signature (even surname-only) except final-signature sheet. First-page lacking signature (containing only preliminary-checks: witness/testator identification, testator will-intention) cannot constitute deed-defect since regarding these elements testator-attention unnecessary via signature. Contesting preliminary-activity requires forgery-complaint filing. Will annullable Art. 67 RD 89/1913 violation complaint rejected; alleged publication-deed timing-falsity (5:30pm referring notary publication-operations not testator-signing time) irrelevant to will-form signing-time. Publication-deed time-indication refers notary reading-deed to appearing-person (defendant) who signed with notary 5:30pm, not will-form testator-signing. Ten-minute drafting (12:30-12:40) insufficient concluding inadequate deceased-wishes investigation by public-official rendering deed-annullable. Public-will validity requires notary asking testator re-expressing wishes before form-reading presence-witnesses; time-difference between testamentary-dispositions receipt-operations and document-preparation-operations permitted; operations may occur outside single-timeframe without validity-affecting. Alleged virtual-general nullity (concrete-cause ascertainment-failure supporting deceased-will) unfounded. Public-deed per Art. 2700 constitutes full-proof until forgery-challenged regarding public-official statements/certified facts including signature-authenticity and obvious-perceptible incapacity-signs absence. Notary required ascertaining testator valid-will-expression capacity per Arts. 47/58 Law 89/1913; failing must refuse duties-performance. Public-will form itself leads excluding perceptible testator-incapacity symptoms; mental-health state although deemed/declared by notary due apparent-incapacity-signs lack may be challenged by any-evidence without forgery-complaint need; implies testamentary-capacity assessment not subject public-faith constraint. Art. 591(2)(3): incapable-making-wills includes those although non-interdicted proven for any-reason even-temporary incapable understanding/willing at will-making time. Incapacity-notion presupposes understanding/will-expression inability consisting either mental-infirmity serious-enough constituting interdiction-grounds (although undeclared) or milder-infirmity nevertheless preventing action-significance understanding. Not-necessary constant-incapacity state; temporary/transitory-incapacity relevant if exists at testamento-factio time. Inability-understanding/intending clouds entire testator-determination capacity rendering entire-will invalid. Will-contester must prove testator-incapacity state at asset-disposition time; capacity constitutes rule, incapacity exception (Cass. 28758/2017). Annulment requires rigorous-proof that will-drafting time testator mental/physical-health state completely-suppressed conscious/free decision-ability; insufficient that normal will-formation/expression process somehow-altered/disturbed due age/serious-illness. Strict burden-proof waived only if deceased previously-suffering serious-permanent mental-illness; then challenger proves illness-existence while will-beneficiary proves lucid-period existence at testament-expression time. Public-will annulment-request requires proving deceased despite showing no obvious-incapacity signs was will-drafting time completely-unaware actions unable forming/expressing own-will regarding asset-destination. Plaintiff failed meeting burden; medical-documentation (nursing-home admission 7.9-7.10.2019, emergency-room reports 6.9.2019, hospital-admissions 9.10-19.11.2019 and 2.12.2019) insufficient proving alleged will-time incapacity. Emergency-reports state patient alert/oriented/cooperative; nursing-home admission-records state lucid/oriented/cooperative; discharge-letter states alert-consciousness state; subsequent-hospitalization discharge-letter highlights patient knowingly-refused echoendoscopy investigating neoplastic-mass, inferring perfect independent important-decision capability even healthcare-field. Medical-documentation shows typical elderly-person physical-problems, not health-problems affecting cognitive-abilities; deceased sufficient understanding/affairs-determination capacity will-time. Medical-psychiatric expert inadmissible as entirely-exploratory. Plaintiff albeit not specifically-requesting Art. 1418 nullity as Art. 643 circumvention-consequence briefly-alleged constituent-elements presence; completeness-sake noted plaintiff provided no summary-description of alleged-offense conduct beyond will-drafting defendant-favor absent legitimate-descendants. Constituent-elements not proven even presumptively. ID: ITI113; Instance_Type: First instance; Legal_Duration: P3Y3M; Law: IT – Civil Code – 606(2), 591(2)(3)
